comment: The table of `del(s, d)` and the release-only bit (D17.9, spec/fir.md 9.4): the operands of
`del` and the two lists of `del` calls in src/fort/check.ft, the mark of an expression in
parentheses (src/fort/parser.ft), which a drop may not carry, the drain that
src/fort/fir_lower.ft writes, the events, the walk and the errors of
src/fort/fir/release.ft, the bit in a build (src/fort/gen_fir.ft), under --check and under
--fir, and the option --span-del-report (src/fort/driver.ft). Each row breaks one rule. The
first stage runs the module suites of the checker, the lowering and the bit, which hold the
count and the position of each error and the FIR of each drain. The second runs the driver
test, which holds the error in each build mode, under --check and under --fir, and the lines
of --span-del-report. The third runs the fail and the run tests of the form, whose goldens
hold the notes and whose runs hold the order of the drops. The table runs in the Linux VM with
the debug preset and the default runner. The md5 guard reads the product compiler. The build
waits 2 s and touches the sources in the guest first, as tools/mutations/use_fort.json does.
The first round of a run can read stale (notes/testing.md 7), so the first two rows are rows
that a full run caught. The row D17.9-store-global needs FIR text: the lowering stores into a
global through an address that it takes first, so only the case `globals` of
test/fort/fir/release_test.ft stores into a global place with no address before it, and the
same case holds D17.9-store-field, a store through a pointer and then a field in one place.
The rows D17.9-constant-temporary, D17.9-each-block, D17.9-constant-first,
D17.9-check-verdict, D17.9-build-verdict and D17.9-store-field come from the review of the
first version, which ran them on a darwin host.
build: sleep 2 && touch src/fort/check.ft src/fort/fir_lower.ft src/fort/fir/release.ft src/fort/gen_fir.ft src/fort/driver.ft src/fort/parser.ft && cmake --build build/Linux/debug --target fort

stages.name: the module suites of the drain
stages.command: python3 test/lang/run_tests.py --root test/fort --fort build/Linux/debug/fort --std-dir build/Linux/debug/std --timeout 1500 -j 4 check_drop_test fir/release_test fir_lower_own_test

stages.name: the driver test
stages.command: python3 test/lang/run_tests.py --root test/fort --fort build/Linux/debug/fort --std-dir build/Linux/debug/std --timeout 1500 -j 2 driver_test

stages.name: the fail and run tests of the drain
stages.command: python3 test/lang/run_tests.py --fort build/Linux/debug/fort --std-dir build/Linux/debug/std --timeout 1500 -j 4 fail/ownership/091 fail/ownership/092 fail/ownership/093 fail/ownership/094 fail/ownership/095 fail/modules/034 fail/casts/048 run/ownership/075 run/ownership/076 run/ownership/077 run/modules/drop

mutations.what: no drop is an error, also one that is not release-only
no `del(s, d)` joins the list of drains, so no drop is decided
`del` takes three operands
each `own` span is a span of owners, a span of `i32` among them
the first operand of `del(s, d)` can be a span with no owner or a pointer
the drop can be a function value in a local
the drop can have another type than `fn (E) void`
a `del(s, d)` that cannot empty its operand joins the list of drains
no one-operand `del` of a span of owners joins the list of --span-del-report
`del(s, d)` frees the storage and drops no element
the drain runs on the place of `s` and does not move the span out first

mutations.old:
fir.operand one = int_const(wide, false, 1);
    assign(lw, counter, fir.rvalue_binary(lw->f, fir.rvalue_kind.rv_add, index, one), at);
mutations.new:
fir.operand one = int_const(wide, false, 2);
    assign(lw, counter, fir.rvalue_binary(lw->f, fir.rvalue_kind.rv_add, index, one), at);
mutations.what: the drain drops every second element
no store breaks the bit

mutations.old: bool memory = s->place.base == fir.base_kind.bk_global || fir.place_indirect(f, s->place);
mutations.what: a store of an owner into a global keeps the bit
a store of a value with no owner through memory breaks the bit
a temporary that one statement fills with an allocation counts as a constant
a store of the zero value of an aggregate through memory breaks the bit
a call of an extern reads as a call of a function with no body, and its note changes

mutations.new:
if (s->kind == fir.stmt_kind.st_assign && s->value.kind == fir.rvalue_kind.rv_call
                && s->value.callee != fir.callee_kind.cl_value) {
mutations.what: a call through a function value keeps the bit
a call of a function with no body in the build keeps the bit
a caller of a function that is not release-only keeps the bit
a build decides no drop
--check decides no drop
--span-del-report writes no line
a named local that one statement fills with a constant counts as a constant
scan reads only the first block of each function
the last fill of a temporary decides whether it is a constant
--check reports a drop that is not release-only but keeps its verdict
a build reports a drop that is not release-only but writes its output

mutations.old: bool memory = s->place.base == fir.base_kind.bk_global || fir.place_indirect(f, s->place);
mutations.new:
bool memory = s->place.base == fir.base_kind.bk_global || fir.place_indirect(f, s->place)
        && s->place.proj_len == 1;
mutations.what: a store through a pointer and then a field does not count
a literal with members counts as a constant
--fir and --fir-after decide no drop
--fir reports a drop that is not release-only but writes the FIR
a drop in parentheses passes
the parser marks no expression in parentheses, so a drop in parentheses passes
